newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk mayor investigated for Islamist state remark.
newsitem.headline: Turk mayor investigated for Islamist state remark.

text.p: Turkish prosecutors on Monday began investigating an Islamist mayor over remarks that it was only a matter of time before the secular republic would give way to an Islamist rule of "justice".
"The prosecutor has begun in inquiry," the governor of the conservative province of Kayseri, Mevlut Cetinkaya, told the state-run Anatolian news agency.
"Don't look at how smart (Western) I look and think I am a secularist," the daily Sabah quoted Kayseri Mayor Sukru Karatepe as saying. His remarks were widely quoted by newspapers on Monday.

"This system must change. But until the (Islamist) reign of justice comes along we will have to take part in these ceremonies," said Karatepe, a member of the Welfare Party whose leader, Necmettin Erbakan, is modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister.

Karatepe was speaking to Welfare Party officials on Sunday, the 58th anniversary of the death Kemal Ataturk, who founded the secular Turkish republic 73 years ago from the ashes of the Moslem-based Ottoman Empire.
Ataturk is accorded demi-god status today, and his picture adorns public spaces and even private offices throughout the country. Insulting him is a criminal offence.

Karatepe was quoted by newspapers as saying he was being "torn apart inside" when he paid his respects to Ataturk, placing a wreath at the foot of a statue and observing a minute's silence at the hour of Ataturk's death.

Governor Cetinkaya told Anatolian the state prosecutor in Kayseri had begun to collect recordings of the offending remarks and other "evidence" against Karatepe, with a view to pressing charges. He did not elaborate.
